normal_signature: Granular, aggregate-based surface texture (asphalt or concrete)
Consistent, stochastic distribution of small stones and binder
Uniform color palette within a single image (grey, beige, or brown)
Absence of large, continuous geometric shapes or foreign objects
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural cracking: Linear fissures or spiderweb patterns indicating material fatigue or settling
Surface potholes or spalling: Deep depressions or chunks of material missing, creating sharp shadows and voids
Foreign object intrusion: Presence of debris, trash, or vegetation that does not match the aggregate texture
Staining or fluid leakage: Irregular dark patches or oily sheens indicating chemical spills or water pooling
rules: if the image contains distinct, continuous linear features (cracks) that cut across the texture, then lean anomaly
if the image contains a large, dark, irregular void or depression (pothole) disrupting the surface continuity, then lean anomaly
if the image contains a distinct object with a color or shape significantly different from the surrounding aggregate (e.g., trash, leaves), then lean anomaly
if the image shows a localized, high-contrast dark patch with a smooth or glossy texture (stain), then lean anomaly
if the image displays a uniform, stochastic distribution of small particles without distinct geometric defects, then lean normal
if the image shows only minor, natural variations in aggregate density or color, then lean normal

normal_signature: Uniform light gray to off-white surface color
Fine, consistent granular texture across the entire field
Randomly distributed, small, dark speckles (pores or aggregate)
Absence of large-scale geometric patterns or distinct objects
Subtle, low-contrast tonal variations without sharp boundaries
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Surface contamination: accumulation of foreign matter like oil, dust, or biological growth (mold) creating distinct patches
Structural damage: cracks, fissures, or chips in the wall material disrupting the continuous texture
Material defects: large voids, exposed aggregate, or uneven curing resulting in significant color or texture deviations
Foreign object intrusion: presence of non-wall items such as screws, wires, or debris attached to the surface
rules: if the image contains sharp, linear discontinuities or jagged edges then lean anomaly
if the image shows distinct, localized patches of color significantly darker or lighter than the background then lean anomaly
if the image contains recognizable geometric shapes or distinct objects not part of the texture then lean anomaly
if the image displays a continuous, fine-grained texture with only random, small speckles then lean normal
if the image shows a uniform color palette with only subtle, low-contrast variations then lean normal

normal_signature: Uniform light gray or off-white surface coloration
Fine, consistent granular texture resembling concrete or stucco
Absence of large, distinct foreign objects or debris
Randomly distributed micro-pores and minor surface irregularities
No visible structural cracks or deep fissures
hypothesized_anomaly_modes: Structural cracking: Linear fractures indicating material stress or settling
Surface contamination: Presence of foreign debris, stains, or biological growth (mold/moss)
Material degradation: Pitting, spalling, or exposed aggregate where the surface layer has eroded
Discoloration: Localized dark spots or patches indicating water damage or chemical reaction
rules: if the image contains distinct linear cracks or fissures then lean anomaly
if the image shows large, non-textural foreign objects or debris then lean anomaly
if the image exhibits localized dark staining or significant color deviation from the base gray then lean anomaly
if the image shows deep pitting or exposed aggregate inconsistent with the fine grain then lean anomaly
if the texture is uniformly granular with only micro-pores and no structural breaks then lean normal
if the color is consistent with the reference gray/white palette without distinct spots then lean normal
